Iteration Structures
Part 1: For Loops
For loops execute a block of code a
set number of times, or for each
instance in a set of data.

Iteration Structure Overview
Instead of writing the same statements over and over, an iteration structure
can execute the same code repeatedly based on a condition or a collection
of values.
Each repetition of the loop is called an iteration.
Iteration structures are useful whenever a task needs to be performed more
than once.
They are commonly implemented using statements such as for and while.
Without iteration structures, many common programming tasks would
require significantly more code and be much harder to maintain.
Learning to use iteration structures effectively is an important step toward
automating repetitive tasks and solving more complex problems.

For Loops
For Loop: An iteration structure that repeats a code block for each value
in a sequence.
A for loop is an iteration structure that repeats a code block for each
value in a sequence.
It is commonly used when the number of iterations is known in advance
or when processing every item in a collection.
Because for loops automatically move from one value to the next, they
are often simpler to use than other loop types.
